title: Phone Interpreter Services: Pros, Cons & Gaps
summary: Learn where phone interpreter services work well in healthcare, where OPI falls short, and how to compare connection time, audio quality, rare-language access, and AI alternatives.
body_markdown:
###


Phone interpreter services connect patients and healthcare staff with a human interpreter by audio, usually through a phone, speakerphone, or conference call.


###


OPI requires little hardware, works across many locations, supports patient calls well, and gives healthcare teams access to human interpreters without on-site staffing.


###


Phone interpretation removes visual cues and can be harder for multi-person conversations, noisy rooms, brief bedside interactions, and languages with longer connection times.


###


OPI works well when the communication is mainly verbal and a human interpreter is preferred, including scheduling, follow-up calls, routine visits, and care coordination.


###


Phone interpretation requires a human interpreter to connect to the call. AI medical interpretation can begin immediately when the language is supported, which can reduce connection delay for short and frequent clinical interactions.
